newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil down on commercial selling, meal up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil down on commercial selling, meal up.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures were lower on commerical selling at midsession Monday, and soymeal futures were higher with soybeans and on fund buying, traders said.
"The commercials are selling the (soy) oil," said one floor trader.
ADM, Cargill and Continental Grain were all sellers of soyoil in early trade, dealers said.
Soymeal futures rose in response to commodity fund buying and on spillover strength from soybeans, traders said.
CBOT soybeans were higher on USDA data showing only a slight improvement in the crop despite beneficial rains.
In early soymeal trade, Smith Barney bought 500 lots December and 200 lots of August, pit sources said.

In export markets, Asian traders said China bought 30,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal for December/January shipment and Egypt bought 21,000 of sunflowerseed oil for shipment during the second half of September, sources said.
At 1109 CDT, December soyoil was 0.03 cent per lb lower at 22.75 and others were down 0.03 to 0.04. December soymeal was up $4.60 per ton at $203.30 and other months were up $3.10 to $5.10.
